ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, B is at the lower left, A is at the lower right, C is above, D is located on line segment BC, and A and D are connected. Reasoning: Let x = ∠ACB. Because D is on line segment BC, BD and BC are collinear, and ∠ABD = ∠ABC = 45°. In triangle ABD, ∠DAB = 15°, therefore ∠ADB = 180° - 45° - 15° = 120°. By the sine theorem, AB/BD = sin120°/sin15°. Also because 2BD = CD, so CD = 2BD, BC = BD + CD = 3BD, thus AB/BC = AB/(3BD) = sin120°/(3sin15°). In triangle ABC, ∠BAC = 180° - 45° - x = 135° - x. Again by the sine theorem, AB/BC = sin x / sin(135° - x). So sin x / sin(135° - x) = sin120°/(3sin15°). Substituting x = 75°, the left side is sin75°/sin60°, the right side is sin120°/(3sin15°), the two are equal; and this ratio corresponds to a unique solution within 0° < x < 135°. Therefore x = 75°.

raw_record.question_text: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC = 45^\circ$. Point $D$ is on $\overline{BC}$ so that $2 \cdot BD = CD$ and $\angle DAB = 15^\circ$. Find $\angle ACB$.

method.method_draft: Use a sine-rule ratio comparison. Read from the diagram/text that D lies on segment BC, so BD and CD are collinear and BC = BD + CD. Let x = angle ACB. Since angle ABC = 45° and D is on BC, angle ABD = 45°. In triangle ABD, angle DAB = 15°, so angle ADB = 120°. Apply the sine rule in triangle ABD to get AB/BD = sin120°/sin15°. From 2BD = CD, get BC = 3BD, hence AB/BC = sin120°/(3sin15°). Now apply the sine rule in triangle ABC: AB/BC = sin x / sin(135° - x), because angle BAC = 180° - 45° - x = 135° - x. Solve sin x / sin(135° - x) = sin120°/(3sin15°), which gives x = 75°.

method.method_draft: Normalize lengths and compute the target angle through side lengths. From the text/diagram, set BD = 1, so CD = 2 and BC = 3. Since D lies on BC, angle ABD = 45°. In triangle ABD, angles at A and B are 15° and 45°, so angle ADB = 120°. By the sine rule, AD/BD = sin45°/sin15°, so AD = sqrt(3) + 1. Because B, D, C are collinear, angle ADC = 180° - angle ADB = 60°. Now use the law of cosines in triangle ADC with AD = sqrt(3)+1, DC = 2, and included angle ADC = 60° to compute AC^2 = AD^2 + DC^2 - 2(AD)(DC)cos60° = 6, so AC = sqrt(6). Finally use the law of cosines in triangle ADC to find angle ACD, which equals angle ACB because D lies on BC. Compute cos angle ACD = (AC^2 + DC^2 - AD^2)/(2AC·DC) = cos75°, so angle ACB = 75°.
method.CoT_raw: Image description: The diagram shows triangle ABC with B at the lower left, A at the lower right, C above, D lying on segment BC, and segment AD drawn inside the triangle. Reasoning: Normalize the lengths by setting BD = 1. Since 2·BD = CD, we get CD = 2 and BC = 3. Because D lies on BC, ray BD is along ray BC, so ∠ABD = ∠ABC = 45°. In triangle ABD, ∠DAB = 15° and ∠ABD = 45°, hence ∠ADB = 180° − 15° − 45° = 120°. By the sine rule in triangle ABD, AD/BD = sin45°/sin15°, so AD = sin45°/sin15° = √3 + 1. Since B, D, C are collinear, ∠ADC = 180° − ∠ADB = 60°. Now in triangle ADC, AD = √3 + 1, DC = 2, and included angle ∠ADC = 60°. By the law of cosines, AC² = AD² + DC² − 2(AD)(DC)cos60° = (√3 + 1)² + 2² − 2(√3 + 1)(2)(1/2) = 6, so AC = √6. Finally, by the law of cosines in triangle ADC, cos∠ACD = (AC² + DC² − AD²)/(2·AC·DC) = (6 + 4 − (√3 + 1)²)/(2·√6·2) = cos75°. Since D lies on BC, ∠ACD = ∠ACB. Therefore ∠ACB = 75°.
